We have the template details. The mapped_rxn is provided:

'Br[Br:7].[O:1]=[N+:2]([O-:3])[c:4]1[cH:5][cH:6][c:8]2[c:9]([cH:10]1)[CH2:11][CH2:12][C:13]1([CH2:14][CH2:15][CH2:16]1)[O:17]2>>[O:1]=[N+:2]([O-:3])[c:4]1[cH:5][c:6]([Br:7])[c:8]2[c:9]([cH:10]1)[CH2:11][CH2:12][C:13]1([CH2:14][CH2:15][CH2:16]1)[O:17]2'

Now we need to apply this template to the target molecule (the product). The product SMILES is the right side of the mapped reaction: after >>. That is:

[O:1]=[N+:2]([O-:3])[c:4]1[cH:5][c:6]([Br:7])[c:8]2[c:9]([cH:10]1)[CH2:11][CH2:12][C:13]1([CH2:14][CH2:15][CH2:16]1)[O:17]2

We need to get the SMILES without atom mapping. Remove atom map numbers and brackets. Let's convert to a SMILES string. The product is a brominated aromatic heterocycle? Let's try to reconstruct: O=N(O) attached to aromatic ring etc. The SMILES likely: O=[N+]([O-])c1c c(Br) c2c(c1)CC C1(CC C1)O2? Need to be precise.

Better to use the tool apply_template with the target molecule SMILES and template ID 1914398. But we need target SMILES. Could derive from mapped_rxn: the product side after >> includes atom map numbers. The tool apply_template likely expects a SMILES without mapping. We can try to feed the product SMILES with mapping? Might still work? Usually apply_template expects a SMILES of product (no mapping). We can try to use the product side stripped of mapping.

Let's construct product SMILES: O=[N+]([O-])c1c c(Br) c2c(c1)CC C1(CC C1)O2

Specifically: O=[N+]([O-])c1c c(Br) c2c(c1)CC C1(CC C1)O2

But need correct aromatic notation: c1c c(Br) c2c(c1)CC C1(CC C1)O2

Let's write: O=[N+]([O-])c1c c(Br) c2c(c1)CC C1(CC C1)O2

Simplify: O=[N+]([O-])c1c c(Br) c2c(c1)CC C1(CC C1)O2

But there may be missing bonds. The original mapping: [c:4]1[cH:5][c:6]([Br:7])[c:8]2[c:9]([cH:10]1)[CH2:11][CH2:12][C:13]1([CH2:14][CH2:15][CH2:16]1)[O:17]2

So aromatic ring fused with a bicyclic aliphatic ring. The SMILES likely: O=[N+]([O-])c1c c(Br) c2c(c1)CC C1(CC C1)O2

Let's generate: O=[N+]([O-])c1c c(Br) c2c(c1)CC C1(CC C1)O2

But need proper closure numbers: c1c c(Br) c2c(c1)CC C1(CC C1)O2

Write as: O=[N+]([O-])c1c c(Br) c2c(c1)CC C1(CC C1)O2

Actually need to include aromatic bonds: c1c c(Br) c2c(c1)CC C1(CC C1)O2

Let's produce final SMILES: O=[N+]([O-])c1c c(Br) c2c(c1)CC C1(CC C1)O2

But there are spaces; remove spaces: O=[N+]([O-])c1cc(Br)c2c(c1)CC C1(CC C1)O2 -> need to remove spaces: O=[N+]([O-])c1cc(Br)c2c(c1)CC C1(CC C1)O2

Also need to join: O=[N+]([O-])c1cc(Br)c2c(c1)CC C1(CC C1)O2 -> there is a space before C1. Should be ...c2c(c1)CC C1... Actually the aliphatic part: [CH2:11][CH2:12][C:13]1([CH2:14][CH2:15][CH2:16]1)[O:17]2

So after aromatic c2, there is a carbon (C) attached to O2 closure. The SMILES: c2c(c1)CC C1(CC C1)O2. That is: c2c(c1)CC C1(CC C1)O2. Remove spaces: c2c(c1)CCC1(CC C1)O2? Wait.

Let's write stepwise: aromatic c2 attached to aliphatic carbon (C) which is part of a ring 1 that also includes three CH2s and closes to O2.

Thus: c2c(c1)C C C1(CC C1)O2. So maybe: c2c(c1)CC C1(CC C1)O2 -> "c2c(c1)CC C1(CC C1)O2". Remove spaces: c2c(c1)CCC1(CC C1)O2? Actually there are three CH2: CH2-CH2-C (C is quaternary). So chain: -CH2-CH2-C1(...). So after aromatic c2, there is CH2 (C) then CH2 then C1. So "c2c(c1)CC C1". That's "c2c(c1)CC C1". So "c2c(c1)CC C1" -> "c2c(c1)CCC1". Then inside parentheses: (CC C1) meaning two CH2 then close to same C1? Actually [C:13]1([CH2:14][CH2:15][CH2:16]1) means a carbon (C13) that is part of ring 1, and attached to a three-membered chain that also closes to same ring 1 (makes a cyclobutane?). So C13 is a carbon that is part of a 4-membered ring? Hard.

Given complexity, maybe easier: use apply_template tool directly with product SMILES containing mapping? Might work. Let's try using the product side as given (including mapping) but remove the mapping numbers and brackets. Could use the mapped_rxn to get product SMILES with mapping removed: we can programmatically strip [*:digit] but not possible here. Could just feed the product side with mapping removed manually: "[O:1]=[N+:2]([O-:3])[c:4]1[cH:5][c:6]([Br:7])[c:8]2[c:9]([cH:10]1)[CH2:11][CH2:12][C:13]1([CH2:14][CH2:15][CH2:16]1)[O:17]2". Remove the atom map tags like [O:1] -> O, [N+:2] -> [N+], [O-:3] -> [O-], [c:4] -> c, [cH:5] -> c, [c:6] -> c, [Br:7] -> Br, [c:8] -> c, [c:9] -> c, [cH:10] -> c, [CH2:11] -> C, [CH2:12] -> C, [C:13] -> C, [CH2:14] -> C, [CH2:15] -> C, [CH2:16] -> C, [O:17] -> O.

Thus product SMILES: O=[N+]([O-])c1c c(Br)c2c(c1)CC C1(CC C1)O2? Let's rewrite with proper aromatic: c1c c(Br) c2c(c1)CC C1(CC C1)O2.

So final SMILES: O=[N+]([O-])c1cc(Br)c2c(c1)CC C1(CC C1)O2. Remove spaces: O=[N+]([O-])c1cc(Br)c2c(c1)CCC1(CC C1)O2? Actually we need correct number of C's: after c2c(c1) we have CH2 CH2 C1, so that's "CC C1". That's "CCC1". Then parentheses "(CC C1)" is two CH2 then close to same C1, making "CC C1" -> "CCC1". So overall after aromatic we have "CCC1(CC C1)O2". That seems like "CCC1(CC C1)O2". So product SMILES: O=[N+]([O-])c1cc(Br)c2c(c1)CCC1(CC C1)O2. Remove spaces: O=[N+]([O-])c1cc(Br)c2c(c1)CCC1(CC C1)O2.

But there is still a space in "(CC C1)". Should be "(CCC1)". Actually two CH2 then close to C1: that's "CC C1" -> "CCC1". So parentheses "(CCC1)". So final: O=[N+]([O-])c1cc(Br)c2c(c1)CCC1(CCC1)O2. That seems plausible.

Let's try apply_template with this product SMILES and template ID 1914398.
We'll call apply_template.
